inlines.text: Show that the area of the Reuleaux triangle is

answer.short:
$A=\frac{1}{2}(\pi-\sqrt{3})r^2$.

Add three $\frac{\pi}{3}$ sectors and subtract twice the equilateral triangle's area.
answer.worked:
Each circular segment is a sector of angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$ minus the equilateral triangle. The Reuleaux triangle consists of that triangle and three such segments.
$$\begin{align*}
A_{\triangle}&=\frac{1}{2}r^2\sin\frac{\pi}{3}\\
A_{\triangle}&=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}r^2,\\
A_{\text{sector}}&=\frac{1}{2}r^2\times\frac{\pi}{3}\\
A_{\text{sector}}&=\frac{\pi}{6}r^2.
\end{align*}$$
Thus
$$\begin{align*}
A&=A_{\triangle}+3(A_{\text{sector}}-A_{\triangle})\\
A&=3A_{\text{sector}}-2A_{\triangle}\\
A&=3\times\frac{\pi}{6}r^2-2\times\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}r^2\\
A&=\frac{1}{2}(\pi-\sqrt{3})r^2.
\end{align*}$$
